author: Peter
html: I disagree with Andy Clark. Escaping from that traditional software like interfaces, doesn't make design more usable. Peter

author: Childrens Bikes
html: I disagree with London Sightseeing Tours, there is nothing easy about incorporating W3C standards. Small, medium and large sites with any slightly tedious functionality will struggle to made a site W3C compliant. We all see lots of sites that are XHTML, CSS compliant but very rare do you see others. I was impressed that Virgin Atlantics site is W3C compliant so it is possible.

author: Miadeo
html: I agree with Peter. Interfaces should be standards

author: London Sightseeing Tours
html: Personally speaking W3C standards are quite easy to incorporate but when so many of the BIG corporate sites fail so regularly to be W3C compliant it sets a bad example. I am currently going through my sites making them WCAG compliant and its a big task for me so I can understand why they dont as its going to take a lot of work and therefore a huge cost which wont be gained back... I think. ;o)

author: Forensics
html:
I think W3C is still important, but I doubt the Goog counts that as high as it once did, especially seeing as most major websites are not W3C compliant.

I also agree that the Javascript years are coming - or Web 2.0 years in general.
